subject: Catalyst Health — post-demo hosting/residency follow-up and asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@catalysthealth.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Catalyst Health — post-demo hosting/residency follow-up and asks

Hi Elena — great to meet the team earlier. Quick recap from our call + concrete asks so we’re all aligned. I kept this short and actionable.

Key pain / goals (what you told us):
- Regulatory driver: certain workloads must remain inside Catalyst's US-based VPC and be air-gapped from public internet for PHI processing.
- Data residency: model inputs + logs must stay in your AWS account (us-east-1) with no egress to shared services.
- Ops: on‑prem or private VPC deployment required for clinical inference pipeline; RTO/RPO expectations TBD but lower tolerance for any external service calls.
- Performance: target P99 latency <= 200ms for single-request inference from your clinical app, sustained burst to ~300 rps during morning batch windows.
- Security: KMS integration (customer-managed keys), host-based attestation, and SOC2 + HIPAA evidence required for legal/procurement.

What we will do next (Redwood action items):
1) Share our "Private/VPC network checklist" and a short on‑boarding runbook (attached). Please review the checklist and mark any non-starters. (attachment: catalyst-network-checklist.xlsx)
2) Provide a preliminary pricing/architecture quote for a Dedicated + Private deployment anchored in your account (attachment: redwood-private-pricing-quote.pdf).
3) Pull together SOC2 artifacts and a short security evidence pack for your security team — will send within 3 business days.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra (suggested: Carlos + one network engineer) to walk networking NAT/route table requirements and the expected subnets.

Questions / clarifications for you:
- Is the restricted networking pattern "no outbound internet egress from inference hosts" for all calls, or only for model telemetry/log shipping?
- Do you have a preference for how we integrate KMS (cross-account vs. external HSM proxy)?
- Target procurement window you mentioned on the call — you said Q4 procurement cycle. Can you confirm an expected contract signature month?

Proposed next steps / dates:
- You: share low‑level network diagram & procurement contact by Wed (8/18).
- Us: send checklist + quote + SOC2 pack by Wed (8/18) end of day PT.
- Team call: Tech deep-dive w/ Carlos — propose Thu (8/19) 10:00-10:45 PT.

If any of the summary points above are off, flag them and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll proceed to share attachments now.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: catalyst-network-checklist.xlsx, redwood-private-pricing-quote.pdf

From: Elena Morales <elena@catalysthealth.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@catalysthealth.ai>, procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Catalyst Health — post-demo hosting/residency follow-up and asks

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the clear recap. Quick confirmations from our side: 
- Correct: primary constraint is NO outbound internet egress from inference hosts. Telemetry must be batched and pulled into a protected sink inside our VPC; we cannot accept cross-account telemetry pushing outside.
- KMS: we prefer cross-account CMKs (we manage keys in our account).
- Procurement: aiming to sign in early November (Q4) but we may expedite to late October if legal signs the DPA quickly. Procurement has been looped.

I uploaded our current network diagram (redacted) — see attached: catalyst_net_diagram_v2.pdf. It shows the two candidate subnets (private-1a/1b) and our on-prem VPN termination point. Carlos will be the technical owner for the deep-dive.

Two asks from our infra team before the deep-dive:
1) Can Redwood run a small proof-of-concept in our account with a single GPU host and strict egress controls (no NAT) to validate in-VPC execution? If yes, rough timeline?
2) Please confirm whether Redwood requires any external allowlists (IPs/FQDNs) for license checks or telemetry during normal operation and for the POC.

Elena
Elena Morales
VP, Engineering — Catalyst Health
elena@catalysthealth.ai | +1 617-555-0244

---
Attachment: catalyst_net_diagram_v2.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalyst Health — post-demo hosting/residency follow-up and asks

Hannah / Ben — internal coordination notes and owners: 
- POC in-customer-account: Ops can stand up a single-GPU private instance in their VPC with no NAT (we will rely on SSM & customer-provided bastion for access). Owner: Ben (infra). ETA for POC spin-up after we receive network diagram + IAM role is 5 business days.
- Allowlist requirements: For the POC we should be able to operate with zero external allowlist if customer provides S3 endpoints and KMS cross-account policies. For long-term monitoring we will offer an optional telemetry pull model to their protected sink; that removes outbound egress but requires an agent in their account. Owner: Rachel (security).
- Legal/DPA: Need to escalate standard DPA + HIPAA addendum. Suggest we give legal the SOC2 pack and a short answer matrix for their privacy team. Owner: Hannah to own external comms; I’ll prep the pack template.

Next internal steps (timeline):
1) Rachel: prepare SOC2 + short answer matrix (48 hours).
2) Ben: prepare a POC runbook and estimate (48 hours) — will include IAM role required and the minimal subnet/route expectations. Attached runbook template as starting point.
3) Hannah: schedule deep-dive with Carlos for Thu (8/19) 10:00 PT and include procurement contact.

I will also draft a short internal risk note noting the strict "no egress" requirement and flag that some monitoring choices will require extra work.

- Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: technical-runbook-template.md

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@catalysthealth.ai>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@catalysthealth.ai>, procurement <procurement@catalysthealth.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Catalyst Health — post-demo hosting/residency follow-up and asks

Thanks Elena & Carlos — that all looks good and aligns with our checklist. Quick confirmations and next steps: 
- POC: Ben will coordinate the POC spin-up once we have the IAM role and a completed network diagram (Ben: will ping Carlos for the exact role ARN).
- Allowlist: For the POC, we will not require external allowlist; for production we’ll present a telemetry pull option so there is zero outbound egress.
- Docs: Rachel will send the SOC2 pack and short answer matrix today. I’ll also circulate the preliminary quote + a draft DPA for your legal to review.

I’ve scheduled the technical deep-dive for Thu 8/19 at 10:00 PT — invite sent to Carlos + procurement. If Thu doesn’t work, reply and we’ll propose alternatives.

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
